title: Corn, canned, reduced sodium, cooked with oil

content.title: About
content.content: Canned corn with reduced sodium is cooked in oil, giving it a tender texture and a mild buttery flavor. The product is shelf‑stable and ready to eat straight from the can.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn is one of the most widely cultivated vegetables, grown in over 100 countries.
Canning preserves most B‑vitamins and carotenoids.
Reduced sodium makes the product more suitable for people watching their salt intake.
Cooking in oil enhances absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin E.
Corn provides dietary fiber that supports digestive health.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes regular bowel movements and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin protect the eyes from oxidative stress.

items.title: Source of vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Low sodium combined with healthy fats helps regulate blood pressure.

items.title: Provides magnesium
items.content: Magnesium is essential for normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn.

items.title: Oil content
items.content: The product contains added oil, which may be undesirable on very low‑fat diets.

items.title: Damaged cans
items.content: If the can lid is dented or bulging, discard it due to possible bacterial contamination.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat the corn straight from the can, add it to salads, soups, stews, pasta dishes, or use it as a filling for wraps. It can also be quickly warmed in a skillet.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. Once opened, keep the corn in a sealed container in the refrigerator and consume within 3‑4 days.
